anomalies.observed: The GND1 (logic-side) and GND2 (bus-side) pins of the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 are all connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: GND1 should connect to the logic ground (GND) and GND2 to a separate isolated bus-side ground (e.g., GND_ISO) to maintain galvanic isolation.

evidence.quote: GND [High Power] : ... U10.4(GND1,power_in) U10.5(GND2,power_in) U11.4(GND1,power_in) U11.5(GND2,power_in) ...
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier is shorted, defeating the purpose of the isolated CAN transceivers. This removes galvanic isolation, can cause ground loops, and eliminates protection against common-mode voltages on the CAN buses.

anomalies.observed: U14.5 (~RESET) is tied directly to the GND net.
anomalies.expected: ~RESET should be pulled high (e.g., to SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V) to enable the device, as is done for U13.5 via R18.
anomalies.impact: U14 (SC16IS752) is held in reset permanently, so the serial ports connected to U14 (TX3/RX3 and TX4/RX4) will be non-functional.

anomalies.observed: The VP (VCC) pins of the TPD4E1U06 ESD protection arrays U4 and U23 are left unconnected (no_connect).
anomalies.expected: VP should be connected to a supply rail (e.g., +3V3) to provide rail-to-rail ESD clamping.
anomalies.impact: The ESD protection on the Ethernet lines is ineffective for positive surges, leaving the CM4 Ethernet interface vulnerable to damage.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple anomalies: the isolated CAN transceivers have their logic and bus grounds shorted together, defeating isolation; U14's reset pin is tied to ground, holding it in reset; and the ESD protection arrays U4/U23 have their VCC pins left unconnected.
